predecessors.name: Nayaks of Thanjavur
predecessors.text: the Kaveri delta around Thanjavur, taken by Venkoji (Ekoji I) in 1675-1676

successors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
successors.text: 'the administration of the Thanjavur kingdom was transferred entirely to the British East India Company' under the Treaty of 1799

ledger.x: 1676: Venkoji (Ekoji I), half-brother of Shivaji, makes himself king at Thanjavur.
1762: Thanjavur becomes tributary to the Nawab of Arcot.
1773: 'troops of the Nawab and the East India Company occupied Thanjavur', and Thuljaji was deposed.
1776: Thuljaji is reinstated 'on condition of hosting a British subsidiary garrison'.
1799: the tributary relation to the Nawab ends when the kingdom passes to the Company.
1799: Serfoji II signs the Treaty of 1799 and 'the administration of the Thanjavur kingdom was transferred entirely to the British East India Company'.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

wars.name: Shivaji's southern (Karnataka) expedition
wars.outcome: Shivaji seized Gingee and advanced to the Kaveri; Venkoji negotiated and assigned the land north of the Kollidam to his commander Santaji.

wars.name: Carnatic Wars
wars.outcome: Pratapsingh allied with Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah and the East India Company against the French; no change to Thanjavur's extent is on the page.

wars.name: Occupation of Thanjavur by the Nawab and the Company
wars.outcome: Thanjavur was occupied in 1773 and Thuljaji deposed; he was reinstated in 1776 with a British garrison.

certainty.note: The pages give a kingdom of the Kaveri delta but no boundary and no area; the only river line named is the Kollidam (1677), which is also the northern edge of the shape.
